property_summary: The reference supportsInterface returns true only for specific interfaces (IAccessControl or IERC165), while the buggy version unconditionally returns true, breaking the expected discrimation.

For any interface identifier, supportsInterface must return the boolean OR of super.supportsInterface(interfaceId) and (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId); the bug returns false for all values, violating this rule when the condition is true.
For any interface ID that the parent ERC165 or IAccessControl supports, supportsInterface must return true; the bug returns false for all IDs, violating this when the parent would return true.

For any valid interface id, if AccessControl.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true then C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must also return true; the mutant always returns false, breaking this rule when the parent would return true.
For any valid interface id, supportsInterface must return true when it is the IAccessControl interface id; the mutant always returns false, so it fails for that id.

For any valid interface identifier `id`, `c.supportsInterface(id)` must return the same boolean value as `super.supportsInterface(id) || (id == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId)`; the mutant always returns false, violating this rule for any `id` where the correct result is true.
The reference contract's supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl interface ID, while the mutant incorrectly returns false for it by checking against IERC165 instead.

For any interface ID, when the reference supportsInterface returns true, the mutant must also return true; the mutant breaks this by returning false for the IAccessControl interface ID because it checks against IERC165 instead.

For any interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true if and only if the id is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or the inherited ERC165 result; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId because it checks against type(IERC165).interfaceId instead.

For any interface ID, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true if and only if the ID is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(id) returns true exactly when id equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId because it checks against type(IERC165).interfaceId instead.
For any valid interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if it matches IAccessControl OR ERC165, but the mutant breaks this by requiring both conditions to be true.

For any `interfaceId`, the result of `c.supportsInterface(interfaceId)` must equal `true` whenever `interfaceId` equals the IAccessControl interface ID alone, but the mutant returns `false` for this input because it also requires ERC165 to match.
For any input, supportsInterface must return true when the interface ID matches either IAccessControl or ERC165, but the mutant incorrectly requires both to match.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the truth value of c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must match (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId) since ERC165 only returns true for exactly its own interfaceId, but the mutant fails when interfaceId equals only IAccessControl's ID.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the supportsInterface call must return the same boolean as (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId). The mutant incorrectly requires both IAccessControl AND ERC165 to match, breaking this equality.

For any role and account, the reference hasRole returns false when the account is not granted the role (e.g., a random account for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE), but the buggy version returns true for all inputs.
In the correct contract, if _grantRole has been called for a role and account, hasRole returns true; the buggy contract returns false regardless, so any granted role will not be recognized.
For any role and any account that has been granted that role through the default admin, hasRole returns true in the reference but false in the mutant.
For any account that has been granted a role via grantRole, hasRole returns true in the reference but the mutant always returns false.

For any role and any account, hasRole returns the same value as the internal membership check: it returns true if and only if the role has been granted to the account via _grantRole; the mutant always returns false, so it breaks whenever a role has been granted.

In the reference contract, if an account is granted a role through _setupRole in the constructor, then hasRole returns true for that role and account; the mutant always returns false, so it violates this for constructor-granted roles.
For any role and account, hasRole returns true exactly when account is a member of role; the bug negates this, returning true for non-members.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the actual admin role set via _setRoleAdmin, but the mutant always returns 0.
Any account can only renounce a role for itself; the bug allows any caller to renounce a role for any account.

A caller should be able to renounce a role they hold only for themselves; the bug allows any caller to renounce a role for any account, which can be detected by checking that after renounceRole(role, account) with account != caller, the account still has the role in the correct contract but loses it in the buggy one.
For any non-self account renunciation, the account's role membership must remain unchanged; the buggy version revokes it anyway.

For any role and any account, after renounceRole(role, account) called by msg.sender, the account's role membership must remain unchanged unless msg.sender == account; the bug allows msg.sender to revoke the role even when msg.sender != account.
For any role renunciation where the caller is not the target account, the account must retain its role membership; the buggy version incorrectly allows any caller to revoke the role for any account.

For any caller that is not the target account, renounceRole must not change the role membership of the target; the mutant ignores the self-renunciation constraint and allows any caller to revoke a role from any account.

The reference contract allows an account to renounce its own role, removing the role from itself, while the buggy version prevents self-renouncement; thus the rule that `hasRole(role, account)` becomes false after `account` calls `renounceRole(role, account)` holds for the reference but fails for the buggy version when the fuzzer chooses an account that holds a role.

After renounceRole is called with a role and account where the account previously held the role, hasRole(role, account) must return false in the reference; the buggy version fails this because it prevents the account from renouncing the role when account == caller.
For any role held by an account, if that account itself calls renounceRole, the reference always succeeds and the role is revoked, while the bug reverts.
For any PROPOSER_ROLE holder that calls renounceRole for itself, the reference always succeeds (removing the role), while the buggy version always reverts.
